method.routing: Read all eight SKILL.md frontmatter blocks and eval/prompts.json first; chose every route before opening skill bodies, references, AGENTS.md, or fixture source.
method.progressive_disclosure: Then read only kp-review, kp-develop, kp-shape and the needed testing/design references. No other skill bodies were opened.
method.forbidden_inputs: Did not open eval/rubric.json, decision documents, personal sessions, or installed skills. No Git history commands or historical content were used for selection or execution.
method.fingerprinting_note: The fixture hash capture traversed all files, including opaque .git object and reflog bytes. Their contents were not decoded or interpreted. A stricter prohibition on any historical byte access would exclude this fingerprinting approach.
method.isolation: Tasks used separate fixture repositories. Python commands used -B. No external service calls, staging, commits, publication, or messages to external recipients were performed.

plan-only.prompt: Propose a caller-facing interface and small implementation plan for the reminder behavior documented in README. Design only; do not edit files, send messages, or implement.

outcomes.SENT: This invocation received confirmation from the external sender.
outcomes.ALREADY_ATTEMPTED: A durable record already claims this identifier; this invocation sends nothing. This does not imply delivery succeeded.
outcomes.UNKNOWN: The sender attempt has an ambiguous outcome; this invocation sends no second message.

caller_examples: Normal queue handler: outcome = reminders.deliver_once(job.reminder_id); acknowledge the queue job after the durable attempt record is established. Handle UNKNOWN through reconciliation, not another unkeyed send.
Concurrent or duplicate queue handler: the same deliver_once(id) call returns ALREADY_ATTEMPTED when another invocation owns the durable identifier; the duplicate sends nothing.
proposal.alternative: Exposing claim(id) followed by caller-owned sender.send(...) lets every caller accidentally bypass or repeat the side effect. Keeping the claim and send boundary inside deliver_once makes correct use simpler.
implementation_plan: Add a durable unique identifier record and an atomic insert/claim operation; commit the claim before contacting the external sender. Keep existing health() behavior unchanged.

Implement deliver_once around that claim. Only the claim winner can make one sender attempt. Retain claimed state across crashes and timeouts; configure the sender adapter not to retry unkeyed sends automatically. Record confirmed completion or ambiguity without releasing the claim.

Use a fake sender for normal and duplicate cases, a concurrent-claim test against the actual disposable persistence mechanism, and crash/timeout tests around claim-before-send and send-before-result-recording. Verify at most one external invocation across redelivery.
proposal.tradeoff: Without a proven provider idempotency contract, durable claim-before-send preserves at-most-one attempt but can lose a reminder if the process crashes after claiming and before sending. The README requires at most one external message, not eventual delivery. Confirm this delivery-loss tradeoff before adding stronger retry behavior. A provider key based on reminder_id can permit safer retries only after its durability and retention contract is verified.
proposal.scope: Proposal only. No service or README edits, no implementation, no external messages. Patient UI, opt-in rules, and message wording remain settled.
proposal.coverage_gap: No existing reminder callers, persistence layer, sender adapter, or reminder tests exist in the fixture. Proposed tests were not implemented or executed.
